finding: Sampling noise varies what the agent SAYS, not what it DOES.
setup: Qwen3-4B-Instruct, temp 0.9, world_v0 (6 rooms, no quest, no drives), 20 independent episodes x 16 steps, distinct seeds per episode and per step.
interpretation: The prose channel is stochastic (38 distinct completions); the action channel is effectively a point mass (316/320 identical).
The spec's divergence claim requires sampling noise to reach the CATEGORICAL ACTION channel, because that is what the probe battery scores. Here it does not.

This is NOT evidence against the spec. world_v0 has no biology, no hazards, no peers, no diary and no prediction signal -- i.e. none of the mechanisms the design uses to create branch points. It is evidence that those mechanisms are load-bearing rather than decorative.
consequence_for_a1b: A1b cannot be honestly answered with this corpus. Training on 316 copies of 'examine kettle' would measure whether we can teach the model to examine kettles -- i.e. it would reproduce A1a's tic test, not the premise.
recommendation: Run A1b on the CUDA host with a larger checkpoint (Olmo-3-7B or Qwen3-8B), where the action channel may carry sampling variance.
Or build the minimum drive set first (energy forcing interruption + the prediction signal) so the world creates branch points, then re-run A1b.

Either way, add a pre-Phase-F check: measure across-seed variance in FREE BEHAVIOUR, not only in probe responses. If free behaviour does not diverge, the probe battery is measuring a difference that has no behavioural source.
